jobs.title: Installation Project Manager
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Geotab ® is a global leader in IoT and connected transportation and certified “Great Place to Work™.” We are a company of diverse and talented individuals who work together to help businesses grow and succeed, and increase the safety and sustainability of our communities.

Geotab is advancing security, connecting commercial vehicles to the internet and providing web-based analytics to help customers better manage their fleets. Geotab’s open platform and Geotab Marketplace ®, offering hundreds of third-party solution options, allows both small and large businesses to automate operations by integrating vehicle data with their other data assets. Processing billions of data points a day, Geotab leverages data analytics and machine learning to improve productivity, optimize fleets through the reduction of fuel consumption, enhance driver safety and achieve strong compliance to regulatory changes.

Our team is growing and we’re looking for people who follow their passion, think differently and want to make an impact. Ours is a fast paced, ever changing environment. Geotabbers accept that challenge and are willing to take on new tasks and activities - ones that may not always be described in the initial job description. Join us for a fulfilling career with opportunities to innovate, great benefits, and our fun and inclusive work culture. Reach your full potential with Geotab. To see what it’s like to be a Geotabber, check out our blog and follow us @InsideGeotab on Instagram.

Who You Are:

We are always looking for amazing talent who can contribute to our growth and deliver results! Geotab is seeking an Installation Project Manager who will be responsible for developing and executing customized installation project plans for large-scale fleet customers, ensuring seamless coordination across resellers, vendors, and end users. If you love working at the intersection of technology and logistics — and thrive in a fast-moving environment where your work has direct customer impact — we would love to hear from you!

What You'll Do:

As an Installation Project Manager, your key area of responsibility will be owning end-to-end project delivery for enterprise fleet installation programs across the United States. You will evaluate customer requirements, build detailed and executable project plans, and serve as the primary point of coordination between resellers, vendors, and end users — ensuring every installation stays on track and meets agreed timelines. You will play a key role in helping the team scale to meet growing demand, and will actively contribute to process improvements that automate and streamline the flow of installation work.

To be successful in this role you will be a resourceful problem-solver who is comfortable managing competing priorities in a high-volume, high-stakes environment. You will work closely with Sales, Reseller teams, and internal stakeholders across Product, Hardware Engineering, and Software Engineering — building the cross-functional relationships that keep projects moving and customers satisfied. The ideal candidate brings a strong technical understanding of fleet hardware and installation systems, combined with the organizational discipline to run multiple complex projects simultaneously.

How You'll Make An Impact:

Evaluate customer's needs in relation to installation services
Develop a detailed and executable project plan to meet the desired delivery time frames
Assist in automating the flow of installation work from reseller to vendor to end user
Conduct meetings with customers and vendors to ensure progress on the plan
Work with Product, Hardware Engineering, and Software Engineering to continually improve Geotab products and services
Support Geotab global strategic initiatives
Consistently demonstrate Geotab's Core Values in all daily work and interactions
Contribute to and maintain departmental Wiki documentation

What You'll Bring To This Role:

3–5 years of experience managing vendor relationships in a project context
Background in fleet, logistics,12-volt technical installation or similar industry experience is highly valued
Experience working within a technical or engineering organization, with knowledge of the high-technology industry
Post-Secondary Diploma or Degree in Business, Engineering, Marketing, or a related field; equivalent experience considered
Professional Certification in Project Management (PMP or equivalent) highly valued
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including comfort with delivering presentations and leading customer and vendor meetings
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to make well-judged decisions under pressure
Technical proficiency with Google Workspace (Sheets, Docs, Slides) and similar business software tools

If you got this far, we hope you're feeling excited about this role! Even if you don't feel you meet every single requirement, we still encourage you to apply.

Please note: Geotab does not accept agency resumes and is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes. Please do not forward resumes to Geotab employees.:

Why Job Seekers Choose Geotab:

Flex working arrangements

Home office reimbursement program

Baby bonus & parental leave top up program

Online learning and networking opportunities

Electric vehicle purchase incentive program

Competitive medical and dental benefits

Retirement savings program

The above are offered to full-time permanent employees only

How We Work:

At Geotab, we have adopted a flexible hybrid working model in that we have systems, functions, programs and policies in place to support both in-person and virtual work. However, you are welcomed and encouraged to come into our beautiful, safe, clean offices as often as you like. When working from home, you are required to have a reliable internet connection with at least 50mb DL/10mb UL. Virtual work is supported with cloud-based applications, collaboration tools and asynchronous working. The health and safety of employees are a top priority. We encourage work-life balance and keep the Geotab culture going strong with online social events, chat rooms and gatherings. Join us and help reshape the future of technology!

Geotab verifies candidates' eligibility to work in the United States through E-Verify, an internet-based system operated by U.S. Citizen and Immigration Services.

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
Project Manager – Industrial Machinery

Hunter Foundry Machinery is seeking a Project Manager to join our team in Bensenville, IL. This position will manage multiple customer machine-build projects from the point of sale through design, production, installation, start-up, post-installation support, and final handoff.

Hunter designs and manufactures large, highly automated machines and material-handling systems for the metal casting industry. Each machine project requires close coordination between customers, engineering, purchasing, manufacturing, assembly, service, and leadership to ensure the equipment is designed, built, delivered, and installed successfully.

The Project Manager will serve as the central point of coordination for assigned machine projects and will be responsible for keeping each project on schedule, identifying risks early, driving key decisions, and ensuring all major milestones and stage gates are completed.

This role is designed for an early-career project professional with approximately 2–5 years of experience in industrial machinery, capital equipment, manufacturing, automation, engineering, or another project-based technical environment.

What your day will look like:

Take ownership of customer machine projects following the sale and manage them through completion and handoff.
Develop and maintain a detailed project plan for each machine build, including major milestones, responsibilities, target dates, dependencies, and risks.
Coordinate project kickoff meetings with sales, engineering, manufacturing, purchasing, service, and other key stakeholders.
Review customer specifications, machine requirements, commercial commitments, and project scope to ensure internal teams clearly understand what has been sold.
Coordinate finalization of mechanical, electrical, controls, and other engineering designs.
Track customer drawing and design approvals and ensure required customer sign-offs are received before critical production activities begin.
Coordinate changes to bills of material, machine configurations, components, and specifications based on customer requirements.
Ensure engineering changes and customer-approved modifications are properly documented and communicated to affected departments.
Work closely with purchasing and supply chain to ensure raw materials, purchased components, and long-lead-time items are identified and ordered early enough to support the project schedule.
Track long-lead components and escalate supplier or material risks that could affect machine completion.
Coordinate with production and manufacturing to establish and maintain key fabrication, machining, assembly, electrical, and controls milestones.
Document critical machine-build dates and continuously compare actual progress to the project plan.
Identify schedule risks, resource constraints, design delays, material shortages, and other issues early and coordinate corrective actions.
Maintain an action-item log and ensure open issues have clear owners and completion dates.
Establish and lead regular project-review meetings with engineering, production, purchasing, service, sales, and management.
Use project stage gates to confirm that key requirements have been completed before moving to the next phase of the project.
Provide concise project-status updates to senior management, including schedule, risks, open decisions, customer issues, and required actions.
Coordinate machine inspection, internal testing, factory acceptance testing, and customer acceptance activities.
Ensure punch-list items identified during testing or inspection are documented, assigned, and completed.
Coordinate machine packing, shipping, and delivery schedules with customers and internal logistics personnel.
Develop the installation and commissioning plan for the customer site, including timing, required personnel, equipment, tools, and customer responsibilities.
Coordinate Hunter mechanical, electrical, controls, and service resources required for customer-site installation.
Maintain close communication with the customer before and during installation to ensure site-readiness requirements are understood and completed.
Track installation progress, start-up activities, testing, training, and final customer acceptance.
Manage the post-installation hypercare period to ensure issues identified immediately following start-up are resolved quickly.
Coordinate outstanding warranty, engineering, service, or technical items following installation.
Ensure final project documentation, drawings, specifications, software, manuals, and other required materials are completed and provided as appropriate.
Lead the formal project closeout and transition of the customer from the machine-build team to Hunter’s service and spare-parts support organizations.
Conduct lessons-learned reviews following major projects and identify opportunities to improve future machine builds.
Maintain organized project files, schedules, meeting notes, approvals, action lists, change documentation, and customer communications.
Support continuous improvement of Hunter’s project-management processes, stage gates, documentation, and reporting.

What we are looking for:

Experience managing or coordinating projects in industrial machinery, automation, manufacturing, capital equipment, engineered products, construction, or another technical project environment.
Strong project-planning and organizational skills.
Ability to manage several customer projects simultaneously while maintaining attention to detail.
Ability to build and maintain project schedules, milestone plans, action-item lists, and risk registers.
Strong follow-through and willingness to hold team members accountable for commitments and deadlines.
Comfortable working directly with engineers, manufacturing employees, purchasing personnel, service technicians, salespeople, suppliers, senior management, and customers.
Ability to understand technical information well enough to coordinate mechanical, electrical, controls, production, and supply-chain activities.
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to identify potential schedule or execution problems before they become critical.
Ability to distinguish between routine project issues and items requiring management escalation.
Strong customer-service orientation and the ability to communicate professionally with customers throughout a long equipment-build cycle.
Comfortable discussing schedule delays, design changes, open technical issues, and other challenging project matters with customers and internal teams.
Ability to lead recurring project meetings and keep discussions focused on decisions, responsibilities, and deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to prepare clear project-status reports for management.
Comfortable spending time on the manufacturing floor and around large industrial machinery.
General understanding of manufacturing processes, bills of material, purchasing, production scheduling, machine assembly, and engineering change processes.
Familiarity with long-lead material planning and supplier-management concepts.
Strong attention to documentation, change control, and customer approvals.
Self-motivated, organized, and comfortable operating in an environment where priorities can change quickly.
Willingness to travel to customer facilities during machine installation, commissioning, and project closeout.

Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Engineering Technology, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Project Management, Business, or a closely related field.
Approximately 2–5 years of relevant professional experience in project management, project engineering, manufacturing, machinery, automation, operations, or a related technical environment.
Previous experience coordinating projects involving engineering, purchasing, manufacturing, installation, or customer delivery is strongly preferred.
Experience with industrial machinery, automation equipment, capital equipment, engineered-to-order products, or manufacturing systems is preferred.
Experience developing and maintaining project schedules and tracking project milestones is required.
Familiarity with bills of material, engineering drawings, purchasing, manufacturing processes, and production planning is preferred.
Experience with project-management tools such as Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Monday.com, ERP systems, or similar platforms is preferred.
Strong Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook skills.
Project Management Professional (PMP) or similar certification is not required but may be considered a plus.
Ability to travel as required to support customer installations, start-ups, and project meetings.

Job Type:

Full-Time

About Hunter Foundry Machinery
Hunter Foundry Machinery has been in business for over 60 years and is a world leader in matchplate molding machines and automated mold-handling equipment for the foundry industry. Hunter equipment is designed and manufactured to help foundries improve productivity, consistency, safety, and efficiency through reliable industrial automation.

We serve customers throughout the manufacturing, metal casting, automotive, aerospace, and heavy-industry markets.

This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career project professional who wants to develop expertise managing complex industrial machinery projects from order through installation. The successful candidate will gain hands-on experience across engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, machine assembly, customer communication, installation, commissioning, and aftermarket support while developing into a key project leader within Hunter.

Hunter is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Risk
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Stripe’s mission is to build the economic infrastructure for the internet. Risk and Compliance Engineering builds products to lower Stripe’s financial and regulatory risk at scale, while retaining a best in class user experience. We build user-facing products, and backend platforms to ensure Stripe’s users are compliant with regulatory and financial partner requirements. We protect Stripe’s brand while also protecting the company from financial losses that can put Stripe’s business at risk. The Risk TPM team is crucial to driving programs to address these challenges.

What you’ll do

As a Technical Program Manager in the Risk and Compliance space, you will play a key role across engineering, product, and strategy to drive programs that span across the Risk organization and Stripe. You will be responsible for the successful definition, cross-functional strategy, planning and execution of large-scale technical programs that help to solve complex problems and empower Stripe and our users.

Responsibilities

Execute on technical programs that require deep systems and engineering knowledge.
Partner with Engineering Managers, Product Managers and other cross functional partners to define, scope, and drive large programs to conclusion.
Develop, implement, and iterate on program management techniques, frameworks, and KPIs to achieve goals with well defined success criteria.
Make substantial improvements to how the teams you work with communicate and operate to significantly increase the productivity and efficiency of the teams.
Define and produce high quality written proposals, communications and documentation.
Leverage data and acquired knowledge to drive strategic decisions at an engineering leadership level.
Create widely circulated plans, driving consistency, clarity and building alignment across teams.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

7+ years of software engineering, systems engineering and/or technical program management experience.
Excellent analytical skills; you digest complex information and make recommendations.
You have a track record of providing program management during all phases of software development from kick-off to launch, demonstrating critical thinking, challenging the norms and thought leadership.
You have very strong written and verbal communication skills, building strong relationships with stakeholders, teams and senior leaders around the organization.
You can drive internal and external process improvements across multiple teams and functions and bring a wealth of experience, opinions, proposals and best practices.
Experience operating autonomously and leading large-scale efforts across multiple teams and functions, with stakeholders in different disciplines across time zones.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in financial risk and compliance
SQL and python scripting and/or programming skills

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $157,700 - $236,500. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

jobs.title: Commercial Solutions Program Manager
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Global Business Services’ (GBS) Commercial Solutions team ensures operational and programmatic excellence across deal cycles, increases revenue through the development of transformative commercial constructs, and drives closure of Stripe’s sold portfolio. The team's reach is widespread across Stripe, not exclusive to one sales segment or geographical region. GBS drives change across go-to-market, positively impacting Stripe users, and cross-functional teams. GBS’s priorities are set through the direction of Stripe leadership and executive vision, partnership with sales and cross-functional organizations, as well as User feedback and market insights. This role sits within Global Business Practices’ Commercial Solutions team, responsible for developing, launching, and maintaining commercial constructs and programs to drive revenue for Stripe.

What you’ll do

Stripe's Global Business Services' Commercial Solutions team is looking for a Commercial Solutions Program Manager to own the end-to-end programmatic development of commercial and GBS launch readiness programs that drive revenue for Stripe. Programs have a large scope and impact in nature, including owning the development and support of first-of-its-kind commercialization efforts, ongoing program support (pre- to post-launch), custom deal support related to the program, ownership of related enablement and communications, as well as acting as a change agent across the business.

You're responsible for the end-to-end management of commercial and GBS launch readiness programs, driving cross-organizational alignment through the delivery of related outputs. This role requires a background in program management and commercial program experience, change management, a strong understanding of private pricing frameworks (and pricing analysis), and experience scaling global, cross-organizational mechanisms.

You have experience in program management ownership, custom pricing strategies, and a background in supporting selling motions. You have strong communication skills and executive presence to effectively communicate with Stripe senior leadership. You'll love this role if you're a natural relationship and mechanism builder.

Responsibilities

Independently lead large scale, cross-functional commercial or GBS launch readiness programs that have Stripe-wide impact, oftentimes first-of-its-kind programs and initiatives
Manage and lead a highly complex program which requires considerable resources and high levels of complex functional and technical integration and knowledge
Support the commercial program deal motion, partnering with Deal Pricing and Deal Strategy Strategists, sellers, and internal stakeholders to solution custom commercial approaches
Work cross-functionally with sales teams, sales leaders, services/support teams, product teams, and cross-functional teams to develop, launch, and scale the commercial program (continuously evolving the ways Stripe goes to market) to support commercialization efforts
Identify, surface, and action systemic, broad issues and gaps, proposing holistic solutions to address root causes
Navigate and propose creative solutions through complex programmatic problems at scale across Go-To-Market and Stripe
Partner with cross-functional teams such as Legal, Finance, Accounting, Service Teams, Product Teams, etc. to resolve and remove internal blockers
Provide coaching for other Commercial Solutions team members, identifying areas to upskill across the function
Act as a liaison within Sales, Deal Pricing and Deal Strategy Strategists, and other stakeholders for custom elements
Facilitate meetings, working sessions, and exercises that assist the leadership team in optimizing effectiveness among themselves and across the organization in general
Advocate on behalf of a position and quickly gain cross-functional alignment on the position
Quickly build credibility and trust with internal stakeholders
Provide strong leadership, communication, and persuasion skills
Lead projects to solve existing commercialization issues

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Lead projects to solve existing commercialization issues

Preferred Qualifications

Direct product launch oversight and experience
Payments industry experience
MBA degree in Business, Technology, Finance, or Economics
Possess a PgMP or PMP certification

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $127,600 - $191,400. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

Kestra Financial is a wealth management platform dedicated to empowering independent financial professionals—including traditional and hybrid RIAs—to grow their businesses and deliver exceptional client service. We combine advanced business management technology with personalized consulting to provide unmatched scale, efficiency, and support. Our advisor-focused culture is built on innovation and advocacy, enabling advisors to offer comprehensive securities and investment advisory solutions to their clients

Lead with Purpose. Partner with Impact

Kestra Financial, a leading provider of wealth management platforms, technology solutions, and investment products empowering independent financial advisors and RIAs nationwide, is seeking a Senior Strategic Implementation Manager.

This role serves as a pivotal execution leader accountable for the disciplined delivery of Kestra Wealth Management’s highest-priority strategic initiatives in investment products and platform capabilities. You will drive the successful launch of new investment products and manage end-to-end launch campaigns while coordinating complex cross-functional projects spanning technology, compliance, business development, and operations.

By implementing and championing agile, Scrum-like cadences and robust portfolio governance practices, you will build transparency, predictability, and accountability across initiatives. Your leadership will ensure that strategic intent translates into measurable business outcomes—including accelerated advisor adoption, revenue contribution from new products, enhanced platform capabilities, and operational excellence.

This is a hands-on, high-impact role for a collaborative leader who thrives at the intersection of strategy, execution, and cross-functional influence in a dynamic, growth-oriented wealth management environment.

What You’ll Do:

Own the end-to-end governance and planning that results in successful delivery of priority investment product launches (e.g., alternative investment solutions, insurance products, or curated offerings) and strategic platform implementation initiatives (new advisory revenue vertical, investment program redesign, etc) from concept through post-launch optimization and benefits realization.
Lead the coordination and execution of comprehensive launch campaigns, aligning go-to-market activities including sales enablement, marketing communications, advisor training and onboarding programs, distribution strategy, and adoption tracking to drive rapid uptake and sustained engagement.
Establish and maintain a prioritized portfolio of strategic initiatives for Investment Platforms & Products; drive rigorous sequencing, capacity alignment, funding discipline, and proactive trade-off decisions (scope, timeline, resources, investment) aligned to Kestra’s business objectives and growth priorities.
Partner with Product Management to translate product strategy and roadmap into executable implementation plans with clear milestones, dependencies, and success criteria.
Support Wealth Management platform and product leads by facilitating high-performing cross-functional project teams and workstreams involving:
Technology: Platform development, data integrations (including MDM/medallion architectures), APIs, advisor portals/tools, and infrastructure enhancements.
Compliance & Legal: Product due diligence, regulatory reviews/approvals, disclosures, risk assessments, and ongoing product governance to ensure adherence to SEC, FINRA, fiduciary, and other requirements.
Business: Commercialization strategy, RIA/advisor engagement and feedback loops, distribution channel readiness, pricing/packaging, and P&L impact modeling.
Operations & Finance: Operational readiness, process design, financial tracking, and benefits measurement.
Map and manage complex dependencies, risks, and interdependencies across teams; proactively identify and remove blockers while fostering alignment and shared ownership in a matrixed environment.
Ensure every initiative incorporates appropriate compliance guardrails, risk controls, audit readiness, and change management from the start.
Design, implement, and continuously mature agile delivery operating models tailored to regulated investment product and platform initiatives. This includes establishing Scrum-like cadences (sprint planning, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews, retrospectives), Kanban for workflow transparency and flow optimization, and scaled frameworks (e.g., program-level planning or release management) for larger or interdependent efforts.
Stand up consistent governance rhythms and forums, including steering committees, launch readiness reviews/tollgates, dependency management sessions, risk reviews, and clear escalation paths to executive leadership.
Drive adoption of modern agile/project tools (Jira, Confluence, Azure DevOps, or equivalent) and best practices to improve delivery velocity, predictability, collaboration, and quality across technology and business teams.
Champion a shift toward iterative, outcome-focused delivery—balancing the need for structure and compliance in product launches with the speed and adaptability required in a competitive wealth tech landscape.
Build and operate a portfolio “control tower” capability: deliver timely, credible, decision-oriented reporting and dashboards on initiative status, milestones, risks/issues, dependencies, financial performance (budget vs. plan, ROI tracking), and leading indicators of business impact.
Define, track, and report on key business outcome metrics tied to each strategic initiative (e.g., new product net flows/AUM/revenue contribution, advisor adoption and usage rates, client/advisor satisfaction or NPS impact, reduction in time-to-market or launch cycle time, compliance adherence, platform feature utilization and engagement).
Proactively surface execution risks, capacity constraints, and recommended trade-offs to senior leadership; lead structured issue resolution, corrective action planning, and recovery efforts to protect delivery commitments and protect/enhance business results.
Prepare and present high-quality materials for executive leadership, steering committees, and governance forums; represent the delivery health and outlook of the Investment Platforms & Products portfolio with clarity and fact-based insights.
Instill a culture of genuine accountability—where teams own and are measured on the delivery of agreed business outcomes and value realization, not merely activity completion or milestone hitting.

What You Bring:

2+ years experience in technical product management in an Agile environment.
5+ years of experience in wealth management, investment operations, or trading
3-5+ years of progressive leadership experience in strategic program/portfolio management, product implementation, launch execution, or enterprise transformation roles within wealth management, RIA platforms, investment product development, fintech, asset/wealth platforms, or similarly complex, regulated financial services environments.

Vitro Automotive Glass operates glass manufacturing plants, fabrication facilities and distribution centers worldwide that are solely focused on the production of automotive glass. This scale allows us to provide the quality and technology required for large volume OEM production, while bringing that same attention to detail and quality to our automotive replacement glass (ARG) operations.

As the needs of the automotive industry rapidly evolve, Vitro stays ahead of the curve to help automakers, distributors and installers meet the ever-changing standards for safety, efficiency and sustainability. It’s not enough just to meet specifications. We are committed to working collaboratively to deliver whatever comes next.

Program Management is responsible for cross-functional management, coordination and delivery of all projects that are assigned to him/her on time and on budget at a level of quality that is acceptable to both Vitro and external customers. The Program Manager has primary responsibility to ensure successful OEM program launches and projects as assigned by the Director. This includes meeting project timelines as specified at acceptable cost and quality to satisfy the needs of both Vitro management and the appropriate OEM customer.

As the only technical expert group within the organization that develops mobile services for corporate clients, we are responsible for the planning, development, maintenance, and vendor management of internal and external systems. Company Description

Continental
is a leading tire manufacturer and industry specialist. Founded in 1871, the company generated sales of €19.7 billion in 2025 and currently employs around 76,000 people in 54 countries and markets.

Tire solutions from the Tires group sector
make mobility safer, smarter, and more sustainable. Its premium portfolio encompasses car, truck, bus, two-wheel, and specialty tires as well as smart solutions and services for fleets and tire retailers. Continental has been delivering top performance for more than 150 years and is one of the world’s largest tire manufacturers. In fiscal 2025, the Tires group sector generated sales of 13.8 billion euros. Continental's tire division currently employs around 53,000 people worldwide and has 19 production and 16 development sites.

HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT

This role provides strategic compliance leadership, coordination, and support across the U.S. PLT and Truck Tire organizations by translating Corporate Compliance requirements into practical, sustainable business processes.

The position is responsible for creating the structure and governance needed for PLT and Truck Tire teams to establish self-audit practices, proactively identify compliance risks, and recommend actions to strengthen controls and business accountability within their respective markets.

Coordinate the implementation and communication of compliance programs, policies, procedures, and guidance.
Support the ongoing development of a strong compliance culture throughout Sales, Marketing, and supporting functions.
Monitor regulatory and corporate compliance requirements affecting the tire business and communicate relevant updates to stakeholders.

Policy & Procedure Management

Ensure business processes align with corporate compliance expectations and documented controls.

Founded in 1971, BNP Associates, Inc. is a full-service consulting and engineering firm specializing in airport and warehousing infrastructure projects worldwide. Over its 55+ years of operation, BNP has completed thousands of projects, ranging from small terminal projects to the world’s largest mechanized material-handling systems.

We are recognized for our leadership in baggage handling systems, checked baggage security screening, aircraft apron systems, air cargo terminals, and construction administration. Our clients include airlines, airports, government agencies, and transportation infrastructure specialists worldwide. BNP serves as a key design partner for complex projects that drive the future of air transportation and logistics.

BNP employs over 220 professionals globally. This position offers an opportunity to contribute to our growth and innovation and work with some of the leading professionals in the field.

BNP is seeking an experienced Project Manager to join our airport systems consulting team, focused on airfield and apron systems projects, including aircraft gate planning, passenger boarding bridge (PBB) programs, and related apron equipment. This role covers the full project lifecycle, from master planning and concept design through construction administration, installation, and commissioning.

This role works closely with clients, contractors, and BNP's internal design and engineering teams to keep projects on schedule, on budget, and aligned with FAA/ICAO/IATA standards. Experience with large-scale hub airport projects.

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. About The Team

Global Business Services’ (GBS) Commercial Solutions team ensures operational and programmatic excellence across deal cycles, increases revenue through the development of transformative commercial constructs, and drives closure of Stripe’s sold portfolio. The team's reach is widespread across Stripe, not exclusive to one sales segment or geographical region. GBS drives change across go-to-market, positively impacting Stripe users, and cross-functional teams. GBS’s priorities are set through the direction of Stripe leadership and executive vision, partnership with sales and cross-functional organizations, as well as User feedback and market insights. This role sits within Global Business Practices’ Commercial Solutions team, responsible for developing, launching, and maintaining commercial constructs and programs to drive revenue for Stripe.

What you’ll do

Stripe's Global Business Services' Commercial Solutions team is looking for a Commercial Solutions Program Manager to own the end-to-end programmatic development of commercial and GBS launch readiness programs that drive revenue for Stripe. Programs have a large scope and impact in nature, including owning the development and support of first-of-its-kind commercialization efforts, ongoing program support (pre- to post-launch), custom deal support related to the program, ownership of related enablement and communications, as well as acting as a change agent across the business.

You're responsible for the end-to-end management of commercial and GBS launch readiness programs, driving cross-organizational alignment through the delivery of related outputs. This role requires a background in program management and commercial program experience, change management, a strong understanding of private pricing frameworks (and pricing analysis), and experience scaling global, cross-organizational mechanisms.

You have experience in program management ownership, custom pricing strategies, and a background in supporting selling motions. You have strong communication skills and executive presence to effectively communicate with Stripe senior leadership. You'll love this role if you're a natural relationship and mechanism builder.

Responsibilities

Independently lead large scale, cross-functional commercial or GBS launch readiness programs that have Stripe-wide impact, oftentimes first-of-its-kind programs and initiatives
Manage and lead a highly complex program which requires considerable resources and high levels of complex functional and technical integration and knowledge
Support the commercial program deal motion, partnering with Deal Pricing and Deal Strategy Strategists, sellers, and internal stakeholders to solution custom commercial approaches
Work cross-functionally with sales teams, sales leaders, services/support teams, product teams, and cross-functional teams to develop, launch, and scale the commercial program (continuously evolving the ways Stripe goes to market) to support commercialization efforts
Identify, surface, and action systemic, broad issues and gaps, proposing holistic solutions to address root causes
Navigate and propose creative solutions through complex programmatic problems at scale across Go-To-Market and Stripe
Partner with cross-functional teams such as Legal, Finance, Accounting, Service Teams, Product Teams, etc. to resolve and remove internal blockers
Provide coaching for other Commercial Solutions team members, identifying areas to upskill across the function

The Senior Project Manager (Sr. PM) assists CAPE in achieving strategic and business objectives by leading project management processes (initiation, planning, executing, monitoring/controlling, and closing) for projects across New Jersey. This Sr. PM role is responsible for both construction and environmental remediation delivery and must be capable of managing field execution, subcontractors, schedules, budgets, safety, quality, and federal documentation requirements.

The Sr. PM integrates all project management knowledge areas (scope, cost, time, quality, safety, resources, communications, risk, procurement, and stakeholder management) so the project functions as a cohesive whole. This position serves as a primary point of contact with clients and agencies and effectively leads teams of scientists, engineers, procurement specialists, subcontractors, field personnel, and other stakeholders to meet CAPE’s financial and performance goals.

This role is onsite at active project locations. Not a remote role.

Key Responsibilities

Lead onsite project execution to deliver scope safely, on schedule, and within budget; develop the execution approach, staffing plan, and phased work plan based on scope and risk.
Build and run the Project Management Plan (scope, schedule, cost, quality, safety, resources, communications, risk, procurement, and stakeholders) and keep plans/baselines current as changes occur.
Control scope using WBS/work packages; manage contract requirements, modifications, and change orders, including impact analysis and timely approvals.
Develop and maintain the integrated schedule (near-term planning through milestones); drive weekly/monthly reporting, corrective actions, and a monthly performance analysis/forecast.
Own project financial performance, cost control, forecasting (ETC/EAC), variance analysis, and recovery plans; identify cost drivers and correct excessive-cost items.
Embed safety and quality into planning and field execution; ensure Safety Plans are in place and followed; maintain incident reporting and a zero-incident culture.
Manage procurement and subcontractors, define and negotiate scopes, oversee performance and invoices, and ensure submittals and progress payments are processed accurately and on time.

Supervise and lead project staff in accordance with company policies and applicable laws; perform other duties as assigned.

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret technical procedures, engineering drawings/specifications, and applicable government regulations (including FAR familiarity).
Strong written and verbal communication skills—able to write clear reports/correspondence and confidently present project status, risks, and decisions to stakeholders.
Persuasive communicator with effective negotiation skills; able to develop strong working relationships with executive management, clients, and subcontractors.
Primavera P6 scheduling experience (required/strongly preferred).

Salary

Up to $160,000 annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Travel

50 % on average

Minimum Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications (Project Manager II) – bachelor’s degree in engineering/science or construction management required. Must have at least three (3) years of progressively responsible related field experience and task management, and two (2) years of onsite Quality Control experience supporting environmental and/or infrastructure work. Must demonstrate a firm grasp of the key project management knowledge areas (scope, schedule, cost, quality, safety, risk, procurement, communications, stakeholders) as determined by management review.
Senior-Level Requirements (in addition to the above) – Minimum ten (10) years of successful project management experience with emphasis on cost, schedule, communications, and resource management on construction and/or environmental remediation projects. Must have a professional certification (PMP, PE, or PG) and a proven track record delivering complex work (including successfully managing at least two (2) projects over $5M). Must have (or be able to obtain) required field credentials including OSHA 30-Hour Construction and 40-hour HAZWOPER with current refreshers.
Tools / Scheduling – Proficient in Microsoft Office and Windows-based systems; strong ability to develop and maintain project schedules. Primavera P6 experience required (or strongly preferred, depending on your HR “required vs preferred” structure).

Preferred Qualifications

Field experience in construction or environmental projects.

WHY CAPE?

For 35 years, CAPE has delivered construction and environmental remediation solutions to governmental and private organizations nationwide. As a $100 M small business, we have Nationwide contracts with the USACE, USN and USAF totaling over $20 B in prime contract capacity. As a top 3 SB in our industry, our $12 B portfolio also includes unrestricted contracts where we compete against large businesses for task order awards. Most recently in the unrestricted area, CAPE won a $30 M + groundwater treatment plant construction project for the USACE in New Jersey. We routinely partner with other small and large businesses to provide better responsiveness in support of achieving our clients’ goals.

Our projects are high-profile environmental remediation projects involving cleanup of contaminated soil, groundwater, and sediment. The culture of our company is one of working together to achieve our clients’ objectives, company goals and employee’s professional goals and is succinctly and accurately defined as “We, Not Me” behavior. To ensure long-term, sustainable growth, we tailor our 3-year vision to be ahead of our industry in delivering our projects, align with our clients and team partners to improve our existing market share and develop new services to support smart growth.

CAPE offers competitive benefits including Medical/Dental/Vision insurance, life insurance, Vanguard retirement savings plan including both traditional and Roth 401(k) with up to 4% match and lowest in class fees, health savings account (HSA) with investment option, flexible spending account (FSA), paid annual leave, paid maternity/paternity leave, and tuition reimbursement. HELP SHAPE THE FUTURE OF CANCER CARE IN CANADA

The Canadian Cancer Society works tirelessly to save lives, improve lives and drive collective action against cancer. Together with patients, volunteers, donors and communities across the country, we raise funds to invest in transformative cancer research, we provide a caring support system for everyone affected by cancer and we advocate to governments to create a healthier future for all. It takes a society to take on cancer – and the Canadian Cancer Society is leading the way

Join an exceptional team of Digital Strategy & Technology professionals helping to power the Canadian Cancer Society’s (CCS) operations and fuel our mission through innovative digital solutions. The Digital Strategy & Technology team is at the forefront of CCS’s digital transformation. Together, they are harnessing digital tools, data and technology to boost fundraising capabilities and enhance the experience of everyone who interacts with us online. With a passion for continuous improvement and a commitment to making an impact, the team ensures CCS’s digital presence is strategic and engaging, helping us inspire and empower more Canadians who care about cancer every day.

MAKING AN IMPACT

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Data Governance and Analytics, the Data Analyst is responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining analytics solutions, reports, and dashboards that support data-driven decision-making across the organization.

Leverage SQL, scripting, and modern analytics platforms to extract, transform, and analyze complex datasets, delivering actionable insights and recommendations that align with business goals
Partner with business and technical teams to translate business requirements into scalable, reliable, and well-governed analytics solutions
Support a culture of data-driven decision-making by applying automation, engineering best practices, and modern design patterns to improve how data is analyzed, visualized, and utilized across the organization

Report & Dashboard Development

Build and optimize semantic models and datasets to support business reporting and analytics needs
Optimize reporting and dashboard assets for usability, performance and accessibility

Data Preparation & Processing

Operational Excellence

DevOps

Quality

Apply development best practices including code quality, documentation, and peer review
Data Governance & Standards

Governance & Compliance

Apply data governance, compliance, and data quality standards when developing analytics solutions
Ensure data accuracy, integrity, and consistency across reporting outputs
Adhere to data privacy, security and compliance requirements (PII, PHI etc.)

Data Standards

Support adherence to established data policies, standards, and best practices
Other

Other duties as assigned

More than 3 years, up to and including 5 years - similar or related general experience in progressively more important positions

Technical Skills

Strong proficiency in SQL for data querying, transformation, and analytical dataset development
Proficiency in Python and/or scripting languages for data analysis and automation
Experience designing and developing reports, dashboards, and visualizations using Salesforce Reporting, Salesforce CRM Analytics and Power BI
Experience building and optimizing semantic models and analytical datasets
Experience working with Fabric to build and manage data pipelines, dataflows, automated workflows, and analytics solutions.
Understanding of data modeling concepts and relational database design

Experience automating reporting, data preparation, and analytics workflows

Experience developing and maintaining automated testing for analytics solutions and reports

Ability to identify trends, patterns, and insights from large and complex datasets
Experience with predictive modeling, statistical analysis, or data-driven segmentation techniques

Strong verbal and written communication skills
Ability to present complex data findings clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders
Experience collaborating across business functions to support data-driven decision-making
Bilingualism (French/English) is highly preferred , with French being an asset due to the organization’s nationwide operations and the need for effective communication across various regions

jobs.title: Operations Program Manager, Tax
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Tax Operations and Delivery team protects user trust by enabling accurate, reliable, and scalable tax operations supporting the TaxJar and Stripe Tax products. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, and cross-functional teams to solve operational challenges, support new capabilities, and continuously improve how tax operations are delivered.

As our products, partnerships, and operational footprint continue to grow, how we execute becomes just as important as what we execute. The Operations Program Management role exists to strengthen how Tax Operations and Delivery plans, coordinates, and delivers strategic work by building repeatable operating mechanisms that improve alignment, clarity, and execution across the team and its partners. If you’re energized by improving how teams work, bringing structure to ambiguity, and building scalable ways for teams to execute together, you’ll have the opportunity to shape the future of Tax Operations.

What you’ll do

We're looking for an Operations Program Manager to help improve how Tax Operations and Delivery executes. You’ll partner across Tax Operations, Product, Engineering, and other cross-functional stakeholders to design and operationalize repeatable execution mechanisms that improve planning, coordination, and delivery for key initiatives.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys bringing structure to ambiguity, simplifying complex organizational challenges, and building practical solutions that improve how teams work together. Your impact will be measured by the repeatable mechanisms you build that make operational excellence easier to achieve across the team.

Responsibilities

Design, maintain, and improve repeatable, lightweight execution mechanisms that track program status, communicate progress, surface execution risks on a regular cadence, and escalate blockers to the appropriate stakeholders.
Partner closely with your immediate Ops team and one or two cross-functional leads across Tax Operations, Product, and Engineering to improve cross-functional planning, alignment, and execution of strategic initiatives
Identify execution friction, process gaps, and process breakdowns, and recommend scalable improvements that strengthen operational effectiveness
Establish meaningful metrics and reporting that provide visibility into execution health and support data-informed decision making
Facilitate cross-functional reviews, planning sessions, and execution forums that help teams align, resolve blockers, and deliver measurable outcomes
Monitor initiatives through rollout, evaluate outcomes, and drive follow-up improvements or remediation where needed

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

3+ years of demonstrated experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives from ambiguity to execution
Demonstrated ability to identify friction and design scalable improvements that drive measurable outcomes
Strong structured problem-solving and diagnostic thinking skills, with the ability to investigate issues, identify root causes, and design scalable solutions
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders and drive alignment without direct authority
Experience designing or improving operational processes, governance, or execution mechanisms that increased organizational effectiveness

Preferred Qualifications

Experience partnering closely with Product, Engineering, and Operations teams
Experience establishing operating rhythms, planning processes, or organizational governance
Experience in a high-growth SaaS, fintech, or operationally complex environment
Familiarity with operational readiness, launch management, or change management practices
Experience using operational metrics to measure execution health and drive continuous improvement
Experience with AI, automation, or workflow tools to improve organizational effectiveness
Lean Six Sigma, continuous improvement, or systems thinking experience

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $101,800 - $152,800. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

About This Role

Wells Fargo is seeking a Cash Management Operations Assistant to join our EMEA Cash Management Operations team in London.

In this role, you will support the day-to-day management of cash, liquidity, and funding activities across EMEA entities. Working closely with Treasury, Operations, and business partners across the bank, you will help ensure the efficient management of payment flows, funding requirements, nostro accounts, and Treasury reporting within a strong risk and control environment.

This is an excellent opportunity to gain broad exposure to Treasury Operations, liquidity management, and cash management processes while developing your career within one of the world's leading financial institutions.

At Wells Fargo, you'll work alongside experienced Treasury and Operations professionals in a collaborative and inclusive environment. You'll gain exposure to critical banking infrastructure, develop expertise in liquidity and cash management, and have opportunities to grow your career through challenging work, continuous learning, and global partnership across the organization.

In This Role, You Will

Monitor daily cash positions and nostro account activity, identifying and escalating exceptions, funding requirements, and unusual transactions.
Support Treasury teams by providing timely information on payment flows, liquidity positions, and daily funding needs.
Assist in managing end-of-day account balances and work with Operations partners to resolve outstanding items.
Provide visibility of significant transactions and emerging issues to senior team members and stakeholders.
Support funding activities across EMEA entities to facilitate the timely settlement of payments and obligations.
Contribute to liquidity management activities, including monitoring and reducing excess cash balances.
Prepare and distribute daily cash flow reporting and management information to Treasury teams.
Produce key operational and management reporting, including support for FX risk and control reporting.
Perform system controls and reconciliations to ensure the accuracy and integrity of cash management data.
Support the opening and maintenance of correspondent banking and nostro accounts in partnership with Treasury and Network Management teams.
Adhere to established risk and control procedures, escalating issues appropriately and contributing to a strong governance framework.
Participate in audits, regulatory reviews, control testing, and risk management activities.
Support process improvement initiatives, operational efficiencies, and change management projects.

Required Qualifications

Experience in cash management, treasury operations, commercial banking operations, loan servicing, or a related financial services environment, or equivalent demonstrated through a combination of work experience, training, and education.
Strong attention to detail with the ability to work accurately in a controlled operational environment.
Effective verbal and written communication skills with the ability to build relationships across teams.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, and confidence working with operational data.
Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
Ability to work effectively under pressure in a fast-paced environment.
Demonstrated problem-solving skills and a proactive approach to identifying and resolving issues.
Basic knowledge of banking products, payments, liquidity management, or Treasury processes is desirable.
Self-motivated, adaptable, and committed to continuous learning and professional development.
Strong team player with a collaborative mindset and a commitment to delivering excellent service to internal stakeholders.

Desired Attributes

Interest in developing a career within Treasury Operations or Cash Management.
Understanding of operational risk and control principles within a banking environment.
Experience supporting process improvement or operational efficiency initiatives.
Ability to work collaboratively across multiple functions and contribute to a positive, inclusive team culture.

Our team is growing and we’re looking for people who follow their passion, think differently and want to make an impact. Ours is a fast paced, ever changing environment. Geotabbers accept that challenge and are willing to take on new tasks and activities - ones that may not always be described in the initial job description. new_jobs.description:
Project Manager – Industrial Machinery

Hunter Foundry Machinery is seeking a Project Manager to join our team in Bensenville, IL. This position will manage multiple customer machine-build projects from the point of sale through design, production, installation, start-up, post-installation support, and final handoff.

Hunter designs and manufactures large, highly automated machines and material-handling systems for the metal casting industry. Each machine project requires close coordination between customers, engineering, purchasing, manufacturing, assembly, service, and leadership to ensure the equipment is designed, built, delivered, and installed successfully.

The Project Manager will serve as the central point of coordination for assigned machine projects and will be responsible for keeping each project on schedule, identifying risks early, driving key decisions, and ensuring all major milestones and stage gates are completed.

This role is designed for an early-career project professional with approximately 2–5 years of experience in industrial machinery, capital equipment, manufacturing, automation, engineering, or another project-based technical environment.

What your day will look like:

Take ownership of customer machine projects following the sale and manage them through completion and handoff.
Develop and maintain a detailed project plan for each machine build, including major milestones, responsibilities, target dates, dependencies, and risks.
Coordinate project kickoff meetings with sales, engineering, manufacturing, purchasing, service, and other key stakeholders.
Review customer specifications, machine requirements, commercial commitments, and project scope to ensure internal teams clearly understand what has been sold.
Coordinate finalization of mechanical, electrical, controls, and other engineering designs.
Track customer drawing and design approvals and ensure required customer sign-offs are received before critical production activities begin.
Coordinate changes to bills of material, machine configurations, components, and specifications based on customer requirements.
Ensure engineering changes and customer-approved modifications are properly documented and communicated to affected departments.
Work closely with purchasing and supply chain to ensure raw materials, purchased components, and long-lead-time items are identified and ordered early enough to support the project schedule.
Track long-lead components and escalate supplier or material risks that could affect machine completion.
Coordinate with production and manufacturing to establish and maintain key fabrication, machining, assembly, electrical, and controls milestones.
Document critical machine-build dates and continuously compare actual progress to the project plan.
Identify schedule risks, resource constraints, design delays, material shortages, and other issues early and coordinate corrective actions.
Maintain an action-item log and ensure open issues have clear owners and completion dates.
Establish and lead regular project-review meetings with engineering, production, purchasing, service, sales, and management.
Use project stage gates to confirm that key requirements have been completed before moving to the next phase of the project.
Provide concise project-status updates to senior management, including schedule, risks, open decisions, customer issues, and required actions.
Coordinate machine inspection, internal testing, factory acceptance testing, and customer acceptance activities.
Ensure punch-list items identified during testing or inspection are documented, assigned, and completed.
Coordinate machine packing, shipping, and delivery schedules with customers and internal logistics personnel.
Develop the installation and commissioning plan for the customer site, including timing, required personnel, equipment, tools, and customer responsibilities.
Coordinate Hunter mechanical, electrical, controls, and service resources required for customer-site installation.
Maintain close communication with the customer before and during installation to ensure site-readiness requirements are understood and completed.
Track installation progress, start-up activities, testing, training, and final customer acceptance.
Manage the post-installation hypercare period to ensure issues identified immediately following start-up are resolved quickly.
Coordinate outstanding warranty, engineering, service, or technical items following installation.
Ensure final project documentation, drawings, specifications, software, manuals, and other required materials are completed and provided as appropriate.
Lead the formal project closeout and transition of the customer from the machine-build team to Hunter’s service and spare-parts support organizations.
Conduct lessons-learned reviews following major projects and identify opportunities to improve future machine builds.
Maintain organized project files, schedules, meeting notes, approvals, action lists, change documentation, and customer communications.
Support continuous improvement of Hunter’s project-management processes, stage gates, documentation, and reporting.

What we are looking for:

Experience managing or coordinating projects in industrial machinery, automation, manufacturing, capital equipment, engineered products, construction, or another technical project environment.
Strong project-planning and organizational skills.
Ability to manage several customer projects simultaneously while maintaining attention to detail.
Ability to build and maintain project schedules, milestone plans, action-item lists, and risk registers.
Strong follow-through and willingness to hold team members accountable for commitments and deadlines.
Comfortable working directly with engineers, manufacturing employees, purchasing personnel, service technicians, salespeople, suppliers, senior management, and customers.
Ability to understand technical information well enough to coordinate mechanical, electrical, controls, production, and supply-chain activities.
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to identify potential schedule or execution problems before they become critical.
Ability to distinguish between routine project issues and items requiring management escalation.
Strong customer-service orientation and the ability to communicate professionally with customers throughout a long equipment-build cycle.
Comfortable discussing schedule delays, design changes, open technical issues, and other challenging project matters with customers and internal teams.
Ability to lead recurring project meetings and keep discussions focused on decisions, responsibilities, and deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to prepare clear project-status reports for management.
Comfortable spending time on the manufacturing floor and around large industrial machinery.
General understanding of manufacturing processes, bills of material, purchasing, production scheduling, machine assembly, and engineering change processes.
Familiarity with long-lead material planning and supplier-management concepts.
Strong attention to documentation, change control, and customer approvals.
Self-motivated, organized, and comfortable operating in an environment where priorities can change quickly.
Willingness to travel to customer facilities during machine installation, commissioning, and project closeout.

Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Engineering Technology, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Project Management, Business, or a closely related field.
Approximately 2–5 years of relevant professional experience in project management, project engineering, manufacturing, machinery, automation, operations, or a related technical environment.
Previous experience coordinating projects involving engineering, purchasing, manufacturing, installation, or customer delivery is strongly preferred.
Experience with industrial machinery, automation equipment, capital equipment, engineered-to-order products, or manufacturing systems is preferred.
Experience developing and maintaining project schedules and tracking project milestones is required.
Familiarity with bills of material, engineering drawings, purchasing, manufacturing processes, and production planning is preferred.
Experience with project-management tools such as Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Monday.com, ERP systems, or similar platforms is preferred.
Strong Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook skills.
Project Management Professional (PMP) or similar certification is not required but may be considered a plus.
Ability to travel as required to support customer installations, start-ups, and project meetings.

Job Type:

Full-Time

About Hunter Foundry Machinery
Hunter Foundry Machinery has been in business for over 60 years and is a world leader in matchplate molding machines and automated mold-handling equipment for the foundry industry. Hunter equipment is designed and manufactured to help foundries improve productivity, consistency, safety, and efficiency through reliable industrial automation.

We serve customers throughout the manufacturing, metal casting, automotive, aerospace, and heavy-industry markets.

This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career project professional who wants to develop expertise managing complex industrial machinery projects from order through installation. The successful candidate will gain hands-on experience across engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, machine assembly, customer communication, installation, commissioning, and aftermarket support while developing into a key project leader within Hunter.
